newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Ben & Jerry's new CEO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ben & Jerry's new CEO.

text.p: Perry Odak, the new Chief Executive Officer of Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc, said he believes the company can resume its growth despite the flat market for superpremium ice cream.

"I think there's a real opportunity for this company to regain its momentum and move forward despite the (competitive) market," Odak told Reuters in a telephone interview from Ben & Jerry's South Burlington, Vt. headquarters.

Odak, 51, most recently served as chief operating officer in a consulting capacity for nine months at U.S. Repeating Arms Co, which manufacturs sporting rifles and shotguns, a spokesman for the company said.

He also held senior management positions at Dellwood Foods, Armour-Dial, and Jovan Inc over the past 25 years. He was named CEO of Ben & Jerry's earlier today, replacing Robert Holland, who resigned in September.
Wall Street greeted the news by sending shares of Ben & Jerry's, up 1/2 to 11-3/8 in light trading on Nasdaq. The stock had traded as high as 19-1/2 during the past year.

Odak joins a company which has been unsuccessful recently at using its strong brand name to grow. The super-premium ice cream category has been flat for years as consumers have turned to low-fat and no-fat desserts, and Ben & Jerry's has been losing market share to Grand Metropolitan Plc's Haagen-Dazs.

Ben & Jerry's announced last fall it would report a loss of from $0.13 to $0.17 per share in the seasonally-weak fourth quarter due to competition from Haagen-Dazs and costs from promotions and the expansion into Europe.
Odak said he signed a three-year agreement with the company paying $300,000 a year. He plans to move to Vermont from his home in York, Pa.
Odak declined to talk about the Ben & Jerry's plans to grow, but stressed his experience working overseas and with entrepreneurial owners.

"I understand transitions and I believe I am good at working with companies through transitions. This company is going through a transition, being very entrepreneurial to having more of balance...inside the company," he said.
